newsitem.title: UK: Atlantis Investment launches new Korea fund.
newsitem.headline: Atlantis Investment launches new Korea fund.

text.p: Britain's Atlantis Investment Management on Monday launched an open-ended investment company to manage a portfolio of equity and debt on the Korean Stock Exchange, a company statement said.

It said the new firm, to be called Atlantis Korea Fund Inc, would be incorporated in the Virgin Islands, where it will pay no tax. Its shares would be dollar-denominated and trade on the Dublin Stock Exchange.
The intial offer period for the fund would last until dealing in its shares began on November 27, the statement said.

"There will be flexibility to move up and down the capitalisation scale, although the fund is expected to maintain a portfolio of 50 to 60 stocks out of a universe of 700 stocks traded on the Korean Stock Exchange, of which 300 are actively traded," the statement said.
The fund may also invest in derivative instruments, lower beta stocks, convertibles and domestic investment trusts, it said. The fund would normally be fully invested and up to 10-percent geared.
Atlantis launched the Atlantis Japan Growth Fund earlier this year, which raised $200 million, and the Atlantis Korean Smaller Companies Fund in June 1995, which raised $100 million.
"Over the first year, we'd be quite pleased with $50 million in the Korea Fund," a senior Atlantis official said.

Atlantis' Korea Fund manager Peter Irving said "Although Korea has suffered like other markets in Asia from the downturn in world demand for goods, the stock market has discounted most of the bad news, leaving certain stocks and certain sectors looking extremely cheap and presenting outstanding value."
